question: The excitatory postsynaptic potentials:
analysis: Excitatory postsynaptic potentials (EPSPs) are graded potentials that occur when neurotransmitters bind to receptors on the postsynaptic neuron, causing depolarization. Unlike action potentials, EPSPs are not all-or-nothing; they are graded and can summate, meaning they can be added together to reach the threshold for triggering an action potential. EPSPs are not hyperpolarizing; they are depolarizing. They do not spread long distances as they decay over time and distance. EPSPs do not have a refractory period, which is a characteristic of action potentials.
